# Independent review of the transcript knowledge extension

This records an independent AI-agent audit, not human annotation, outside expert
endorsement or conference acceptance. Its scope is the unchanged 493-document
Channel Lab frame (1,411,446 words, 26 publisher contexts). There is no claim to
have listened to every recording or closely read every retained passage.

## Milestone 1 — evidence and prospective test contract

The independent reviewer froze twelve information needs from inspected passages
in twelve documents and ten publisher contexts, plus four ambiguity/evidence
sufficiency controls, before viewing any new retrieval rankings. The private
query artifact SHA-256 is
`27f6917ea6c2a52569b7ec8ec4b6d9ba06be583342822ecfa24de63ea70d4da8`.
Every known support has a selected-body hash, exact character interval and span
hash. Prior accepted readings informed most selections; one Crimson Circle
passage was newly read. This is a purposeful source-informed diagnostic, not a
blind benchmark, human ground truth, a trained holdout or an estimate of general
answer accuracy. Other sources remain unjudged. A known-source hit alone cannot
establish that the retrieved passage includes the required qualification.

The four controls test ambiguous labels and insufficient evidence. They do not
assert that an exhaustive semantic census proved absence. Relevant background
may be returned without licensing a synthesized arrival date, an authenticated
entity, independent extraterrestrial proof or a personal probability.

The methods contract fixes full-source lexical and MiniLM retrieval, private
500-word passage BM25 collapsed to sources, and top-50 reciprocal-rank fusion
with constant 60 and the unchanged MiniLM tail. All methods share the 493-source
universe. These cutoffs precede execution; no tuning on diagnostic outcomes is
allowed. The previous knowledge-bank experiment showed that unrestricted
full-list fusion with a partial card index mechanically promoted card-covered
sources. That failed design must not recur. The present primary comparison
contains no card index; its remaining passage-length, masking and representation
confounds must remain visible.

Concrete admission requirements:

- Printed documentary question/response turns, uncertain punctuation cues and
  generated study prompts have different types. A following span is context
  until there is a documentary answer boundary. Unknown ASR voices cannot be
  promoted to verified speakers or audience questions.
- Refusals, corrections, conditional alternatives and referent scope stay with
  the evidence. A hypothetical classroom prompt, quoted question or interviewer
  transition must not automatically become a confidently answered question.
- Source-local extraction coverage is different from close-reading coverage.
  Summaries and automatic outlines need stated construction, selected-edition
  bindings and locators; model-written questions are not transcript quotations.
- Publisher/creator contexts and printed claimed labels are provenance, not
  authenticated people or beings. Graph edges must state whether they encode
  publication, label attribution, documentary adjacency, paraphrase support,
  lexical mixture or computed similarity. Shared labels do not prove identity,
  agreement, influence or contradiction.
- Public metadata/paraphrase search and private full-transcript search are
  different collections. Public downloads must omit source bodies, private
  evidence text, paths and raw media. Filters, graph denominators, exports and
  search scopes must agree.

The reviewer asked the extraction owner to freeze policy and inspect varied hard
cases before full processing; the curation owner independently froze its reading
selection without seeing the diagnostic questions. Retrieval controls are not
scored as negative relevance examples.

## Milestone 2 — executed evidence and arithmetic

The seven-source corrected pilot passed before full extraction. The reviewer
found that arbitrary ASR newlines reduced a complete Crimson Circle question to
“of enlightenment?” and caused another prompt to be skipped. The owner corrected
the punctuation boundary policy; the actual full prompts and a regression test
were checked before the 493-source run. Refusals, a singular/plural correction,
quoted questions and rhetorical prompts were inspected without assigning
unverified speakers or inventing answers. A separately copied completed pilot
with one changed private-bank byte was rejected by the corrected resume gate.

The full run passed independent body/artifact normalization, 19,335 exact support
span checks, public/private projection reconciliation and count/type checks.
All 2,523 documentary Ra pairs were rebuilt from original printed turns. An
independent character scanner reproduced all 6,408 punctuation candidates in the
other 387 sources, including two skipped nonlexical punctuation units. There are
493 generated reading prompts, making 9,424 automatic records. Every source's
lexical keywords and factor weights match the prior frozen analysis. These checks
verify the specified extraction rule, not candidate precision or recognition
accuracy. Zero documentary pairs outside Ra is a boundary-recognition limit,
not evidence that those recordings contain no audience or interview questions.

Curation release 02 passed all 82 exact evidence-span/artifact checks, 27 card
and 26 question joins, and eight unchanged legacy-card comparisons. Independent
token-set unions reproduced 11,290 newly read words, 10,006 prior words and 2,794
legacy support words: 22,042 unique words across 42 sources after overlaps.
The reviewer freshly read nine selected hard-case cards' 4,999 support words and
the wider 600-word Ra window. These cover noisy object-name normalization, a
qualified numerical forecast, a quoted confidence joke beside advertising,
self-description versus a channeled persona, refusal to prove an entity exists,
ceremonial divine roles, rejection of a fixed sound/dimension map, recorded sound
gaps and a missing question. Their paraphrases preserve those limits. The other
new cards received provenance checks, not an independent full semantic reading.
The two Lyssa printed questions correctly bind an external publisher Q/A
artifact; the Ra 1.1 question binds the actual extracted record and both exact
question and answer spans. Publication-context notes do not imply close reading
of entire channels.

The private/public database projections passed independent all-row comparison,
493 private body-hash checks and exact reconstruction of all 547 approved public
FTS items. Public body/question/answer/context/evidence text is null and the
public passage table is empty. Seven independently computed combined-filter
memberships and fourteen actual public/private searches passed, including empty
results and operator-like input. The reviewer requested a publication gate that
rejects private SQLite filenames and raw source content hidden under the public
filename; the parent implemented that gate before copying data.

Retrieval arithmetic passed without importing the producer: the reviewer rebuilt
all 3,076 text-position passages in a fresh in-memory FTS5 index, manually
computed query term counts/log TF/frozen IDF/L2, checked saved-vector cosine,
reproduced all 64 complete rankings and top-50 fusion/tail behavior, and checked
all query and publisher-group summaries. Scores reproduced exactly. A separate
cache audit checked the pinned tokenizer, all sixteen masked-input hashes,
378 input wordpieces without truncation, exact vector order and model-manifest
binding. Neural inference was not independently repeated.

Known-support reciprocal-rank means are BM25 0.91667, TF-IDF 0.67083, MiniLM
0.81974 and fusion 0.93333. The publisher-group mean reverses the first and last
ordering: BM25 0.925 versus fusion 0.920. The Council identity information need
places its inspected source first with BM25, sixth with TF-IDF, 284th with
whole-document MiniLM and fifth after fusion. All twelve supports are in BM25's
top three; fusion puts eleven in its top three and twelve in its top five.
These are useful failures and retrieval diagnostics, not evidence of uniform
hybrid superiority, general model quality or answer correctness. Passage extent,
name masking, source length and maximum passage pooling remain confounded.

A second independent review agent rebuilt all 622 typed nodes and 3,664 edges,
checked 27 card/26 question joins and 34 unique card-support spans, and reconciled
GraphML direction/weights. Twenty-four actual one/two-hop/filter cases reproduced
1,083 paths; five invalid cases were rejected. Generated source-to-`asks` edges
were removed before execution. All 9,424 automatic extraction records are
explicitly omitted from this compact graph rather than converted into interpreted
claims. Default navigation includes lexical-factor paths and excludes semantic
neighbors. The graph is provenance/navigation, not causal or answer inference.

## Milestone 3 — corrections and publication

The independent scientific and bounded local UI review passes for the artifacts
listed below. Five additional actual Chromium scenarios used the integrated
release with no request interception or mock data: a channel-filter transition
keeps an explicit out-of-filter reader notice; a two-source comparison retains
both sources with matching-filter flags in its JSON export; the adverse Council
retrieval rank remains visible; an exact printed-label graph/export contains the
independently expected source set; and the graph page fits 320, 390 and 1440 pixel
viewports without page-level horizontal overflow. No page errors occurred.

The reviewer requested clearer multi-source comparison semantics and corrected a
caption that called an information-need category a source family. The implemented
UI now distinguishes the category from actual source-context IDs. A comparison
qualifies when at least one linked source satisfies every source filter; other
comparison sources remain present and are marked outside those filters. This
avoids silently losing comparative evidence or implying a strictly single-source
export. The owner conducts the broader browser, failure and stress suite.

Compact private receipts include `pilot-correction-independent.json`,
`extraction-01-extraction-independent.json`, `punctuation-independent.json`,
`curation-independent.json`, `curation02-join-independent.json`,
`database-independent.json`, `retrieval-independent.json`,
`retrieval-encoding-independent.json`, `graph-independent.json` and
`ui-final-independent.json`. The final independent receipt binds the exact
reviewed files and these proofs. Earlier failed pilot findings remain retained.

There is no unresolved blocker within this review scope. The parent must still
bind the final documentation/UI into the publication manifest, pass its integrated
release gate and verify the deployed page. Local acceptance does not claim that
those later actions have happened. The release remains exploratory: purposeful
readings and queries, unverified ASR and source claims, partial relevance labels,
uncertain speaker roles, no independently repeated neural inference, and no
human-validated answer benchmark or complete-channel census.
